request: How is the Highway Trust Fund financed, and when is it projected to run short of money?

reply.reply:
**The Highway Trust Fund is financed mainly by federal fuel taxes and other transportation excise taxes; its projected end-of-year balance first turns negative in FY2028.**

- The projection shows end-of-year HTF shortfalls beginning in FY2028, reaching $19.55 billion, and growing to $153.99 billion by FY2032. (R47573, PDF p. 12)
- The table projects negative start-of-year HTF balances beginning in FY2029, at -22.29 billion dollars. (R47573, PDF p. 12)
- The HTF is financed by fuel and other transportation-related excise taxes, primarily federal gasoline and diesel taxes at 18.30 and 24.30 cents per gallon, respectively. (R48472, PDF p. 6)
reply.reasoning: CRS reports the primary funding sources as gasoline and diesel taxes. The newest projection we found, based on CBO’s February 2026 baseline, shows a shortfall beginning in FY2028.
